title: "Synthetic Data"
description: "Artificially generated data designed to resemble selected properties of real data or satisfy a defined use."
term: "Synthetic Data"
letter: "S"
category: "Data Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Synthetic data is created rather than collected directly from real-world
events. It can imitate some properties of real examples or represent
scenarios that are difficult, costly, or sensitive to collect.

## Technical explanation

Synthetic datasets may be generated from simulations, probabilistic
programs, generative models, or manually designed rules. Fidelity is
multidimensional: a dataset can match marginal statistics while failing to
preserve important correlations, rare cases, causal structure, or privacy
properties.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Synthetic data can support prototyping, testing, data augmentation, and
privacy-aware development. It can also introduce artifacts or amplify
generator bias, so its usefulness must be measured on the intended
downstream task and compared with real-data evaluation.

## How it works

The team defines the target distribution, constraints, and intended use,
then generates examples with a simulator, model, or rules. Quality checks
compare important statistics and task performance, examine coverage and
failure cases, and test for memorization or leakage where relevant.

## Practical example

A robotics team can simulate rare obstacle configurations to test a
navigation pipeline. The simulations broaden test coverage, but performance
must still be checked in realistic environments because simulated dynamics
may differ from hardware.

## Common misconceptions

- Synthetic data is not automatically unbiased, private, or realistic.
- Similar aggregate statistics do not prove that synthetic examples are
  safe substitutes for real data.
